title: She wept in the night; no comforter from those who loved her
english: Upon the first lament, the one that began from Aleph, we were able to save the wording. But upon this one what would someone say—a city being said to have wept in the night, so that the tears are upon her cheeks—unless perhaps someone will say that those named a city, who also pay tribute, have wept, having been reminded from what sort of peace and freedom into how great a slavery and humiliation they have come? How then shall we also narrate “in the night,” or that in the time of the common rest of all human beings the city, being reminded, while resting wept, and wept with the tears flowing fountain-like upon their cheeks? And the wailing was most stretched out for them and the tears flowed on, there not being even one comforting them from so many who loved them, and everyone who loved setting aside the friendship toward her and having changed into enmity. Who then, as toward the wording, are those who formerly loved her, from whom there was not one who would comfort her? title: Contemplative soul as daughter of Zion; beauty of true doctrines

title: Jerusalem remembers past humiliation when doctrines fall
english: For the one remembering while suffering such-and-such things does not remember the present, but the past. And after a little: Having raised such difficulties in the place and seeking a reminder of her past humiliation and of her rejections—because her people have fallen into a hand of an afflictor and the things brought upon her have come about—we consider whether perhaps humiliation in the proper sense is nothing other than sin, just as exaltation is right practice, and rejection comes about from nothing operating except base action; for this is sufficient to thrust away from God and from everything finest according to nature. When, then, Jerusalem was drunk—that is, those dwelling in her—and beside herself from the sin she was being humbled, she was not delighted in the stumbles; but when her repayments have come through her people having fallen into hands of the afflictor, no one helping her, then she was reminded of the things because of which she was suffering, grasping those as causes both of her people’s having fallen and of her having been left helpless.

title: Uncleanness as obstacle; wash the soul’s feet with Jesus
english: According to the bodily narrative what is said about Jerusalem now is such. Uncleanness is an obstacle for Jerusalem; but of what it is an obstacle, the prophet has left for us to understand. Perhaps it shows that the uncleanness is a hinderer of her journey. And also, being such, it shows that Jerusalem did not remember her last things. And the one who has these before the eyes and sees what will meet him because of the sins will not sin. Because of this uncleanness, then, there is an obstacle for her; and because she does not remember her last things, she brought down her wonderful and great things—which she had when she was worthy to be overseen—and led them into lowliness, though formerly they were oversized and greater than every praise. But also after all these things there was none comforting her: “See, O Lord, my humiliation,” says the speaker, “since the enemy is magnified over what has happened to my homeland.”

And after a little: Yet one must inquire, according to the laws of the ascent-sense, whether it is possible for uncleanness to be in someone who is not its cause. And let us also see the first thoughts of the Lament. Such a soul, having fallen away, is altogether also in uncleanness, which uncleanness hinders walking the holy road. And just as holy Moses and his successor Joshua are commanded by God to loose the sandals when stepping upon a holy place—it not being fitting for the feet to wear dead hide in a holy place—so if someone is going to walk unimpeded, perhaps he ought not only to loose but also to wash off the uncleanness that has come about from the dust around the feet. And we suppose a symbol of this to be that the Savior, having put water into the basin, washed the feet of the disciples, saying to Peter who did not yet understand the mystery and for this reason was hindering: “If I do not wash you, you have no part with me,” and “What I am doing you do not know now, but you will know after these things.” Therefore it will be necessary for the uncleanness around the feet of the soul, so to speak, also to need Jesus, so that he may wash it off and we may be able to have a part with him. For if this remains, it is an obstacle to our walking the road according to the sound word—the Savior who said: “I am the way.”

title: Nations tread the sanctuary; vices enter the soul’s shrine
english: And something most paradoxical Jerusalem suffered at the time of the captivity. For she beheld nations—which God commanded not to enter into the assembly—treading the sanctuary, where not even for the Israelites is it lawful to enter, only the priests having been counted worthy to be in that place after not ordinary purifications. And the enemies reached even as far as the untrodden places, entering into a place which scarcely, after much sanctification, the high priest entered once a year.

And after a little: And if Jerusalem, just as we set out before, is such a soul, one must understand her goods according to nature—being her adornment, through which she was serving the divine—laid away in her places untrodden by everyone except the high-priest Word, to be called her desirable things. And upon all these the enemy who has conquered in wrestling, having afflicted the one not campaigning well for herself but worthily left behind by the divine help, having stretched himself through his operative power unto the base things, has pulled them out of the ruling part and has left desolate of the good things the soul that stood away from God. And nations in this place must be allegorized as the crowd of vices, having entered into the ruling part created to be receptive of God and a true sanctuary of the one wanting to rest upon a pure mind. title: Yoke of impieties; conscience as choking yoke
english: Providence, she says, has not slept over my impieties; for God, as if taking them into hands through examination, has woven them into the works that are for repayment. Wall here, then, is both king and rulers and as many as by power were walling her round—whom he counts worthy to pour unceasing tears of repentance, which the fallen wall throughout procures for those who see. These things, he says, belong to them—even if again he signifies the grief of the power that long ago was guarding, showing this hyperbolically. “And in affliction,” he says, “they remembered the Lord from their whole heart.” Do this, then, he says, weeping night and day and “on your beds be pricked”; and do not consider release from these things to be sobriety; for repentance is unto salvation. And one is sober not by ceasing from good things, but from worse ones. And join the mind continually toward Christ, so that he may guard you as pupil of an eye and may become a wall for you.

title: Night watches; meditate; stay awake for the Lord
english: The night is attentive, the soul being gathered together in it in the quiet of the senses. Then he commands to meditate in the commandments of God and to say with David: “by night I was meditating with my heart, and my spirit was searching.” And the night being divided into four watches, say with David: “my eyes anticipated the watches,” and with Habakkuk: “upon my watch I will stand, and I will look out what the Lord God will speak in me.” For then you will say: “for he will speak peace upon his people.” Meditate, then, in the night of the present age; for “the wrestling is not for you toward blood and flesh, but toward the rulers, toward the authorities”; for “you do not know when the lord of the house comes, late or at midnight or at cock-crow or early; lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.” And again: “for if you had known in what watch the thief comes, you would have stayed awake and would not have let your house be dug through.”
